topic.title: History-order utility in the strongest joint model
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does the supplied order of valid historical events improve click AUC beyond their content in the strongest joint model, and is any benefit justified by measured cost?
topic.hypothesis: The inherited joint history compression and task-conditioned representation may exploit predictive event order, but the supplied evidence does not establish this. Retain the unchanged starting model as the utility control and compare order-preserving and order-invariant treatments with matched-capacity replacements. Any permutation must keep event fields and historical actions aligned, transport each task's eligibility with its event, and preserve padding and every original history restriction. Use only supplied positions, without assuming timestamps, time gaps or unavailable events. Order-dependent predictive information would be supported by a reproducible advantage over controls trained under their corresponding order treatment. Equal or better order-invariant performance would falsify useful order dependence for the tested setting; sensitivity only to prediction-time permutations could instead reflect distribution shift. Separate order effects from capacity, optimization and compute through replacement controls, measured parameters and runtime, and reserved resources for attribution and repetition before assessment. This is an untested local hypothesis, with no novelty or mechanism-confirmation claim.
